Reviewer: MacBook-Pro.local pool job team-skull review-4499, Claude Opus 5.5 (claude-opus-5-5), mkinney; did not write or refresh this PR.

**Verdict: Needs changes before merge.** The code and the recorded programs are correct. One project law is not met (item 1). A body edit or a file move closes it.

This is a SAFETY-tier review: the PR changes posted G-code and the machine check.

## What looks good

- The joint-angle solve is correct. I derived it again by hand: `Rx(A')·Ry(B')·Z = (sin B', -sin A'·cos B', cos A'·cos B')`. So `B' = asin(vx)` and `A' = atan2(-vy, vz)`. The second solution `(A'+180, 180-B')` is also correct.
- The nest rule is correct for each chain type. A head chain puts the parent on the left. A table chain puts the inverse of the work transform on the left, so the rotary nearest the work is outer. In a table-and-head machine, the table is outer.
- The Rust rule (`machine/tilt_chain.rs`) and the JS rule (`post/tilt_chain.rs`) agree. They read the same fields (`parent`, `turnsPart`, `direction`/`axis`, `travel`), they use the same precedence, and they have the same refusal texts. The pinning test compares the posted words with `joint_angles`.
- The stream always gives A, B and C together (`post/cnc.rs:202-206`). Thus a record never gets a B of 0 in place of a modal B.
- `tilt()` writes the joint angles back on the record before `feedWord` and `heldAngles`. Thus the rotary feed cap and the held angles read the posted angles.
- No production code calls `MachineModel::pose` (only the sim tests). Thus no collision check reads stream letters as joint values. This closes the open question under "Not exercised" in the body.
- Only `tilthead.mch` has an A-about-X and B-about-Y pair in `assets/machines/`.
- No `unwrap`/`expect`/`panic!` outside tests. Both new modules have a provenance line. The decision record is present. The commit subjects are conventional. The fixing commit ends with `Fixes #4417`. The body has a `Changelog:` line.

## Goldens moved (checked line by line)

I solved each pose again with an independent script. Each posted value agrees to 3 decimals:

| Pose letters | Posted joint angles | File |
|---|---|---|
| A16.78 B-47.983 | A24.251 B-45.342 | `multiaxis_deburr_tilthead.nc` |
| A-16.78 B-47.983 | A-24.251 (B modal, -45.342) | `multiaxis_deburr_tilthead.nc` |
| A16.78 B47.983 | A24.251 B45.342 | `multiaxis_deburr_tilthead.nc` |
| A-16.78 B47.983 | A-24.251 (B modal, 45.342) | `multiaxis_deburr_tilthead.nc` |
| A30 B30 | A33.69 B25.659 | `examples/catalog/multiaxis/indexed/indexed.nc` |
| A30 B15 | A30.867 B12.953 | `vendor_mch_cli` expectation |
| A-45 B12.25 | A-45.66 B8.629 | `program_units` expectation |

The body lists each changed recorded program. No other `*.nc`, `*.cl` or catalog file changed.

## Mutations (run by me)

1. Restored main's `fanuc.cps` and `doosan-dnm.cps`. Result: RED. Three tests fail: `fanuc_posts_the_joint_angles_of_a_chain_where_a_carries_b`, `doosan_dnm_posts_the_joint_angles_of_a_chain_where_a_carries_b` (line 112, axis mismatch) and `a_chain_with_no_stated_nest_is_refused_by_name`.
2. Made `judge.rs` `pose_problems` judge the letters again (ignore the `joint_angles` result). Result: RED. `the_machine_check_judges_the_joint_angles_not_the_letters` fails (line 179).

I restored the tree after each mutation.

## Results, merged with main (locally, macOS, `upstream/main` 2394b5ad1)

The PR head already contains `upstream/main` 2394b5ad1. The trial merge was "Already up to date".

- `cargo test -p camcraft-post --test tilt_chain_joints`: 6 passed.
- `cargo test -p camcraft-post` (lib and all suites): 1,430 passed, 0 failed. This includes `post_engine` (143), `script_rotary` (66), `script_dialects` (175), `script_goldens` (445) and `script_wcs` (108).
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-post --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-app --tests -- -D warnings`: clean.
- `camcraft-app` suites by name, all green: `example_catalog` (50 passed, 4 ignored), `example_catalog_adaptive`, `example_catalog_edge_work`, `program_units`, `setup_align_multiaxis`, `rotary_verify`, `mcp_multiaxis_deburr`, `mcp_multiaxis_deburr_post`, `tilt`, `post_not_judged`, `opening_rotary_pose`, `approach_rotary_order`, `folder_lists`, `conformance`, `wcs_tilt`, `machine`, `rotary_letter`, `units_in_refusals`, `setup_align_mill_turn`, `first_traverse_mill_turn`, `lathe_cross_drill`, `stock_source_cross_drill`, `drilling_cross_stock`, `drilling_cross_holder`, `drilling_cross_box`, `drill_reach`, `cross_drill_neighbours`, `coarse_cross_drill`.
- `cargo test -p camcraft-app --lib rotary_gate`: 10 passed.
- `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main`: the plan has 728 steps. I ran it for about 20 minutes and then stopped it. Steps 1-121 passed (119 test steps, 0 failed). I did not run the rest of the plan. Above, I ran by name each app suite that reads `tilthead.mch` or builds its own A and B rotaries. The author reports the full plan green on this head (728 steps, 0 failed).
- `cargo xtask gate light`: 4 steps, 0 failed.
- Heavy: not run by me. The author ran the targeted heavy step `app heavy: example_catalog` on this head (1 step, 0 failed), as AGENTS.md "Heavy lanes at review" requires for a P1 PR.

Extra suites run: none were owed. The diff does not touch `testdata/` or the import code.

## Requested before merge

1. `crates/post/tests/tilt_chain_joints.rs`: this is a new top-level test binary. AGENTS.md (**New tests join a directory suite**, #3187) requires a new integration test to join an existing directory suite. A new top-level file needs a one-line reason in the PR body. The body gives no reason. Do one of these:
   - Move the file into `crates/post/tests/script_rotary/` (it holds `upright_after_tilt.rs` and the other rotary post tests). Add `mod tilt_chain_joints;` to `script_rotary/main.rs`. Update the test names in the body and the issue comment.
   - Or add a one-line reason to the PR body. A body-only fix keeps this head, and a re-review of the same head can then be clean.

## Notes (not blocking)

- `crates/post/src/post/js.rs` is now 413 lines (412 on main). It was already over the 400-line limit.
- Merge order: PR #4473 (#4436, sign convention) changes the same G43.4 output in `fanuc.cps` and `doosan-dnm.cps`. The PR that merges second must merge `main` again. Then it must show that the joint-angle solve and the sign rule work together, in the post and in the machine check. The author's comment says the same.
- A table-table chain and a table-and-head chain have no shipped machine and no posting test. The body says so. The rule is correct for the `tool_rh` convention.

A maintainer will approve and merge by hand.
